passage: Nikita had come home to the village for Ganesh Chaturthi after eight months in Pune. At the courtyard well, her mother Tanuja did not look up. "You left us for a salary," she said to the bucket. The neighbours' ears seemed to grow. Nikita's face burned; she wanted to shout that she sent money and called every night. Instead she took the other handle of the bucket and said, "I missed the smell of this courtyard, Aai. I am not coming back to live here, but I will be here every festival, and I will call on Sundays." Tanuja's lips tightened, yet she let Nikita carry the water. That night Tanuja set aside the first modak for her.

qa.q: How long had Nikita been in Pune before the visit?
qa.a: Nikita had been in Pune for eight months.

qa.q: What did Nikita feel and want to do when her mother spoke to the bucket?
qa.a: Her face burned, and she wanted to shout that she sent money and called every night, but she held back.

qa.q: How did Nikita show love while staying firm on her decision?
qa.a: She helped carry the water, promised to be there every festival and call on Sundays, and said she was not coming back to live there.

qa.q: What might Tanuja's setting aside the first modak for Nikita suggest?
qa.a: Tanuja is softening and shows love in her own way, even though her words were sharp.

grounding: A family says the protagonist abandoned them for work; she feels guilt and anger, shows love in ways she can and stays firm on her choice.

passage:
Counselling note, session two. Client: Amandeep, 25, software engineer, recently moved from Amritsar to Bengaluru.

Amandeep said her family calls her every evening. Her mother cries on the phone; her uncle has told relatives she "abandoned her parents for money". Last week her father refused to speak to her on his birthday. She described feeling guilty all day and angry all night. "I send money, I call every day, and I'm still the villain."

Her cousin Vandana, who also moved away for work, has told her this is how it was for her too, for a year.

We discussed ways she can show love that fit her real life: a fixed video call three evenings a week, rather than daily; one visit home every two months; a family photo album she is making for her mother. We also discussed that she does not have to justify her job again in every call.

She left saying, "I can be their daughter and still live here." Next session in two weeks.

qa.a: She moved from Amritsar to Bengaluru.

qa.q: How does Amandeep feel about her family's accusations?
qa.a: Amandeep feels guilty all day and angry all night, as though she is the villain.

qa.q: What ways of showing love did Amandeep and the counsellor discuss?
qa.a: A fixed video call three evenings a week, a visit every two months, and a photo album for her mother, while no longer justifying her job in every call.

qa.q: How might Amandeep's mother feel about the move?
qa.a: Her mother likely feels sad and left behind, which shows in her crying on the phone.

grounding: A counsellor's note shows a young woman whose family says she abandoned them by moving for work, who feels guilt and anger, shows love in ways she can and stays firm on her decision.

passage:
Saturday.

Amma called again today. "You chose him over us. Your father hasn't slept since the wedding." Then Appa took the phone and said nothing at all, just breathed, and handed it back.

It's been six months since I married Arun. Not the boy from Madurai they picked. Arun from Kochi, who makes me laugh and irons my kurtas better than I do. I'm Madhuri, their daughter still, and they talk as if I died.

I cried in the bathroom for an hour. Then I got angry. Then I felt guilty for being angry.

Rehana, my colleague, said, "Love them the way you can. Don't undo your life."

So here's what I'm doing. I'll keep calling every Sunday. I sent Amma the jasmine she likes from the market near our flat. I invited them for Pongal. I will not apologise for marrying Arun.

They may take time. Months, maybe. I can wait. I just won't go backwards.

qa.q: How long has Madhuri been married to Arun?
qa.a: She has been married for six months.

qa.q: What was Madhuri feeling after the call?
qa.a: Madhuri felt guilt and anger in waves, crying in the bathroom for an hour.

qa.q: How is Madhuri showing love while staying firm?
qa.a: She calls every Sunday, sent jasmine, invited her parents for Pongal, and refuses to apologise for marrying Arun.

qa.q: How might Appa be feeling when he breathes silently on the phone?
qa.a: Appa may feel hurt and unable to find words, torn between his anger and missing his daughter.

grounding: A diary entry shows a young woman whose family says she abandoned them by marrying by choice, who feels guilt and anger, shows love in ways she can and stays firm.
